A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLS research, with matching algorithms, theoretical results and original experiments. All 31 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v3, including appendices A-D, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-distribution simulations, speculative-decoding experiments, and Gaussian-source and MNIST compression results in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Llama evaluations, empirical matching-probability measurements, decoding-consistency experiments and CIFAR-10 compression results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1-2, the strongly drafter-invariant variant, compression sampling procedures, and documented neural architectures and losses remain unchanged. The additional evaluations do not document a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds CIFAR-10 compression, extending image coverage from handwritten digits to color natural images. Gaussian sources and all five language datasets are retained. The Llama additions change model configurations rather than language-task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments. The Llama evaluations reuse the corresponding SpecInfer, SpecTr and Daliri comparisons, while CIFAR-10 reuses the compression baseline. The new consistency analysis also uses the existing SpecInfer comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama 2-68M/7B and Llama 3-1B/8B configurations, plus a paired consistency protocol using ROUGE, fixed randomness and drafter temperatures 1.0 versus 0.5. CIFAR-10 introduces 16-by-16 side-information patches. These substantially expand evaluation design. Section 4.4's full-vocabulary statement is not reconciled with Appendix D.1's retained top-50 setting, so a change to the original sampling protocol cannot be established.

E4.justification: New Tables 7-8 examine empirical matching probabilities and LML-bound tightness on actual LLM distributions across draft counts. Appendix D.2 adds quantitative output-consistency tests and a GSM8K case study under temperature changes. These directly investigate practical consequences of the theoretical properties beyond v1's existing efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: The new consistency study specifies paired runs sharing a seed and averaging over four seeds, with uncertainty values in Table 9. Existing five-seed LLM, ten-repeat Gaussian and five-repeat MNIST reporting is retained; no increase in repetitions of those experiments is documented.

E6.justification: Original numerical results remain unchanged, while v3 adds Llama performance, matching probabilities and bounds, ROUGE consistency, CIFAR-10 distortion, and absolute baseline throughput. For example, new Table 9 reports GSM8K ROUGE-L of 0.745 versus SpecInfer's 0.647; Tables 15-16 report CIFAR-10 MSE of 0.0788 versus 0.0956 at K=4 and Lmax=4. These are additional results under newly reported evaluations.

T1.justification: Remark 1 and Appendix A.7 add proofs that the LML bound is exact for point-mass proposals, a single proposal, and identical target/proposal distributions. This supplements the bound's characterization; the main theorems, drafter-invariance definitions and existing derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: GLS and its matching bound, competitive drafter-invariant multi-draft decoding, and improved multi-decoder compression. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability discussion through draft-count computation/memory tradeoffs, vocabulary and alignment limitations, and shared-randomness and floating-point requirements for distributed compression. Appendix D.2 also distinguishes output consistency from output quality and emphasizes that conditional invariance does not guarantee identical outputs.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit code-repository URL, identifies Huggingface Transformers, and documents settings accompanying the Llama and CIFAR-10 additions, including patch dimensions and selected N and beta. Most existing implementation, hardware and training details are unchanged.

R1.justification: New references support the added discussions and experiments, including recursive speculative decoding, Gumbel-top-k sampling, CIFAR-10, ROUGE, Transformers and a speculative-decoding survey. Core positioning relative to Daliri and the matching-lemma literature remains unchanged. DROP was already cited in a v1 footnote.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and most existing prose are retained. Local expansions add practical guidance, two limitations subsections, Appendix A.7, Appendix D.2 and acknowledgements, alongside wording corrections and updated conference text.

P2.justification: Seven new tables substantially expand the displayed evidence: Llama comparisons, empirical matching/bound comparisons, ROUGE consistency and CIFAR-10 results. Existing compression tables are retained and renumbered. Figures remain largely unchanged, with Figure 4 gaining a Rate (bits) axis label and several displays repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps: v1 did not directly measure practical output consistency or compare its bound with empirical matching on real LLM distributions. The new analyses, additional model and image evaluations, exactness proofs and deployment limitations substantially strengthen support for the retained contributions. Reporting flaws temper this gain: Appendix D.2 names NaturalReasoning where Table 9 labels MBPP, and the vocabulary-setting descriptions remain unreconciled. These limit reproducibility of parts of the evidence without outweighing the broader improvement.
